HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 6, 2023
  200 W. BROADWAY
  BILLIE JEAN KING MAIN LIBRARY, 3:30 PM

Julie Lie, Chair  Jeffrey Johnson, Member
Desiree Rew, Vice Chair  Ray Morquecho, Member
Sarah Bedy, Member  Mary Simmons, Member
Pat Chotiswatdi, Member  Susana Sngiem, Member
James Howat, Member

  FINISHED AGENDA & DRAFT MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the Homeless Services Advisory Committee of the City of Long Beach convened
at 3:33 p.m. at Billie Jean King Library. At the start of this meeting, we did not have Quorum. Quorum
was met as 3:44pm.

Pam arrived at 3:44pm, we have a quorum.

ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present: Lie, Rew, Johnson, Howat, Sngiem, Simmons, Chotiswatdi, Bedy

  Commissioners Absent: Morquecho

Also present: Stephanie Sosa, Community Program Specialist, James Howat, Member,
Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, Jennifer Santana, Homeless Services Bureau
Secretary.

Also present: Alvin Teng, Community Program Specialist; Dalton Dorr, Community Program
Specialist.

Chair Julie Lie presiding.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  23-51470  Recommendation to receive and file all Subcommittee updates.

  Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee Update
  Chair Julie Lie and Community Program Specialist Stephanie Sosa provided the
  update.
  • The posted amount for the Mayor’s Fund donation is incorrect, there was a
  discrepancy with Long Beach Community Fund. There was one large
  donation of $100,000, however it no longer shows in the statement. Staff has
  reached out to LBCF for confirmation.
  • At this time, staff believes $9,000 dollars were received for the month of

  Page 1 of 6

  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 6, 2023
  200 W. BROADWAY
  BILLIE JEAN KING MAIN LIBRARY, 3:30 PM

  October and more is expected in the month of November.
  • There are a few pending applicants, additional information has been
  requested on our end.
  • Smaller organizations are applying for the Mayor’s Fund, but we are getting
  more applicants.

  Policy Subcommittee Update
  Subcommittee Chair Sarah Bedy provided the update.
  • The subcommittee met on the second Monday of last month, to continue to
  go over the Safe Sleep Program and how they can campaign for a pilot
  program here in Long Beach to Council.
  • A few members have met with their members to ask for support.
  • Chair Julie spoke about her meeting with Councilmember Duggan and her
  staff and provided their perspective on what they feel is of upmost priority for
  these types of programs, which is public safety. Next week Chair Julie Lie
  and Member Sarah Bedy will meet with Councilmember Zendejas and her
  Chief of Staff.
  • They asked other members to read the article on San Diego’s safe sleep
  site.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Vice Chair Rew, to
  approve recommendation. The motion by the following vote:

  Yes:  5  Lie, Rew, Sngiem, Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Johnson, Howat, Morquecho, Simmons

2.  23-51471  Recommendation to receive and file the presentation on the 2024 Homeless Count
  and the Methodology.

  Alvin Teng, Special Projects Coordinator, presented in person.
  • PIT Count 2024 will be on January 25, 2024
  • This is a comprehensive count and survey of all people experiencing
  homelessness in Long Beach, both sheltered and unsheltered.
  • 2023 PIT Count results, 3,447 people were experiencing homelessness on
  the morning of January 26,2023.
  • Components of the PIT Count include: street-based enumeration conducted
  simultaneously by nearly 300 staff and community volunteers, specialized
  Street-based enumeration count of harder reach areas such as large
  encampments, riverbeds, train tracks, freeway infrastructure, etc., service-
  based access centers count of all people experiencing homelessness who
  utilize service centers such as food programs, social service agencies,

  Page 2 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 6, 2023
  200 W. BROADWAY
  BILLIE JEAN KING MAIN LIBRARY, 3:30 PM

  medical facilities, etc., and housing inventory count of all people
  experiencing homelessness residing in shelters, transitional housing, or
  other residential programs.
  • PIT Count Survey consists of demographic survey, 35-40 survey questions
  including personal ID and visual count where an individual declines to
  respond to a demographic survey or is otherwise inaccessible.
  • Access centers and housing inventory are also accounted for with the help of
  access center staff, city staff provide training and incentives to ensure they
  are counted.
  • City staff expect to release the 2024 PIT Count Data in late April 2024.
  • Ways to support for the count includes volunteers for the count, ensure your
  clients or program participants are counted, and donate towards hygiene
  kits.
  • Members had questions and comments regarding volunteer opportunities,
  PIT processes and requirements for other jurisdictions and the survey.
  • Staff responded.

  A motion was made by Member Sngiem, seconded by Vice Chair Rew, to
  approve recommendation. The motion by the following vote:

  Yes:  5  Lie, Rew, Sngiem, Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Johnson, Howat, Morquecho, Simmons

3.  23-51472  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Proclamation Update.

  Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, presented.
  • The updates to council will be provided monthly, next meeting will be on
  Tuesday.
  • Goals of the emergency is to build overall capacity to improve our approach
  to this systemic societal problem.
  • Efforts to date include:
  o 85 new interim beds with another 120 in planning or construction,
  $63+ million in funding and identified an additional $5.7 million in
  FY24 budget.
  o Permanently housed 582 people through emergency housing
  vouchers.
  o Better communication both internally and externally with our
  counterparts.
  o Improved MAC outreach and increased rate of service acceptance,
  speed up affordable development from 6 to 12 months to 60 to 90
  days.

  Page 3 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 6, 2023
  200 W. BROADWAY
  BILLIE JEAN KING MAIN LIBRARY, 3:30 PM

  o Increased engagement with community and non-profit organizations.
  • Enhanced focus on Safety Downtown, additional MAC locations in
  downtown, increased programming and activation in Lincoln Park and Billie
  Jean King Library, increased police presence with focus on reducing crime
  and enhancing safety, increased cleaning services and maintenance to
  public spaces, and continued efforts to support existing business and
  attraction of new business as well as large scale events.
  • Presentations from Eugene, OR and Denver, CO were heard at the
  Homeless Services Advisory Committee, regarding safe sleep program, the
  HSB is working on a report back to Council on this being a potential model
  for interim housing options, a report will follow in the upcoming months.
  • The process for re-establishing the jail mental health clinician position has
  begun.
  • Data will be refreshed on the Dashboard December 7th
  • Community engagement to discuss the expansion of the Long Beach
  Guaranteed Income program to assist in preventing families from falling into
  homelessness.
  • Finalize operational structure for the emergency shelter to community based
  shared housing.
  • Members had questions about the shadow subsidies, the report on safe
  sleep sites and other potential funding opportunities.
  • Staff responded.

  A motion was made by Member Sngiem, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion by the following vote:

  Yes:  5  Lie, Rew, Sngiem, Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Johnson, Howat, Morquecho, Simmons

4.  23-51473  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff Report.

  Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, presented.
  • Outreach direct phone number, 562-470-4672(4MSC) is live and taking calls.
  o 348 requests for Outreach
  o 211 newly enrolled people in outreach
  o 417 outreach services provided.
  o 310 first-time visitors to the MSC
  o 3,176 total visits in November
  o 167 average daily visits
  o 140 Mobile Access Enrollments
  o 251 Mobile Access Center Services Provided

  Page 4 of 6
   HOMELESS SERVICES ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 6, 2023
  200 W. BROADWAY
  BILLIE JEAN KING MAIN LIBRARY, 3:30 PM

  • For the staffing update
  o 9 staff from Communicable Disease Emergency Response team will
  be reassigned to HSB Staff to support the MAC, Permanent housing,
  and Encampment Resolution
  o Positions that are in recruitment/interview phase: CPS II Homeless
  Court, Health Educator II, Counselor II, Administrative Analyst III & II,
  CPS V (Program Components Coordinator)
  o 4 positions that will begin soon.
  • Community Outreach for tiny homes project has been completed at Spring
  and California including community information session on December 2nd.
  • 40 winter shelter beds added at 702 W. Anaheim.
  • Staff are working on getting things set up for inclement weather site for
  additional beds when it’s raining or cold. Working on site to be finalized next
  week.
  • 2nd phone line counselor is going through training and onboarding currently,
  this will help provide more tele support for those unable to visit the MSC.
  • Encampment Resolution round 2 is staffing up, goal to launch initial
  sheltering efforts in early 2024, with reassignment staff support.
  • Three project-based sites that begun application to lease-up process over
  the past month. These projects are creating over 140 new project-based
  units of permanent supportive housing.
  • Continued work to develop regional plan as part of the HHAP Round 5
  application process.
  • Initial planning and surveying to develop and ERF Round 3 Proposal has
  begun.
  • Staff currently reviewing proposals for a service provider to operate the
  access center.
  • Increased media and solicitation around “the Season of Giving” including call
  for donations to Mayor’s Fund.
  • Members had questions regarding clarification on funding opportunities,
  additional bed numbers and additional programming.
  • Staff responded.

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Vice Chair Rew, to
  approve recommendation. The motion by the following vote:

  Yes:  5  Lie, Rew, Sngiem, Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Johnson, Howat, Morquecho, Simmons
